newsitem.title: USA: New jobless claims down in latest week.
newsitem.headline: New jobless claims down in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans seeking new jobless benefits fell last week, the government said Thursday.
The Labour Department said initial claims dropped to 325,000 in the week ended Feb. 1 from a revised 337,000 in the previouos week.
The less-volatile four-week moving average, considered to be a more reliable gauge of employment trends, fell to 331,000 from 341,250 in the week earlier.
The department said the moving average was at its lowest level since the week ended Nov. 9, 1996, when it stood at 330,500.
Thirty states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Jan. 25, the latest period for which that data are available.
The largest decreases were North Carolina with 11,210, California with 9,051, Pennsylvania with 8,850 and Tennessee with 8,158.
North Carolina, Pennsylvania and Tennessee reported fewer layoffs in various industries, including textile, apparel and electrical equipment. California had fewer layoffs in the service industry.

The department said one state reported an increase in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the week ended Jan.25. Texas, with 4,925 additional claims, reported layoffs in the non-electrical machinery industry.
